Jurbarkas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tauragės apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jurbarkas is first mentioned in a Jewish context in a 1590s rabbinic responsum by R. Meir ben Gedalyah of Lublin. The town's magnificent wooden synagogue, built in 1790, was among the oldest in Lithuania; the famous Hebrew novelist Avraham Mapu, a foundational figure in modern Hebrew literature, once taught at the local talmud-torah after its 1884 curriculum reform. One of the town's two public parks was informally nicknamed 'Tel Aviv,' reflecting the strength of local Zionism. After the June 1941 German invasion, Jews were forced to tear down their own historic wooden synagogue; three days later, its Torah scrolls and religious books were burned, and mass shootings continued until September, when the town's mayor reported no Jews remained.
